- Use the "外國專業人員工作許可申辦網" to submit your application online. [3]
- The application requires a copy of the application form, a copy of the student ID (with school registration stamp or proof of enrollment), a copy of the residence permit and passport, and the receipt of the review fee (NT$100 per case, payable by postal transfer to the Labor Ministry Labor Development Agency hiring permit account 19058848 or via ATM). [3]

- The maximum fine for a student who works without a work permit is NT$150,000. [4]
- If the employer hires a student without a permit, the employer may be fined up to NT$750,000. [4]
- The work permit is valid for up to 6 months. [4]
- For more information, visit the Ministry of Labor website (https://www.wda.gov.tw) or call the Labor Ministry hotline 02-8995-6000. [4]

- The mobile device view of "Work Permit Information" is only used as proof of having a work permit. [1]

- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay for up to two years. [1]
- During this extended stay, they can work without obtaining a separate work permit. [1]
- Family members can also apply to remain in Taiwan during the extended stay. [1]
- The changes simplify the hiring process by eliminating the need for employers to separately apply to the Ministry of Labor for work permits during the extended stay. [1]

- The 1990 hotline for foreigners in Taiwan is 1990. [3]
- It provides consultation services for foreigners and new residents regarding visas, residence, work, education, culture, tax, health insurance, transportation, employment, medical health, personal safety, child upbringing, welfare services, legal information, and other life matters. [3]
- The hotline is available in Chinese, English, Japanese 24 hours a year, and in Vietnamese, Indonesian, Thai, and Cambodian from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday (excluding national holidays and other rest days). [3]
- The hotline is managed by the Immigration Affairs Bureau. [3]

- Call 165 for anti-scam consultation. [1]
- Remember the 3C principle: Calm Down, Check it out, Call 165. [1]

- The fine is 10 times the employment insurance premium for the period the employer failed to register the student worker. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years and at least 128 credits in total. [1]
- The university adopts the system of academic years and course credits. [1]
- Undergraduate students are expected to complete their studies within four years, with no fewer than 128 course credits earned in total. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 for more information: https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 12 extra graduation credits are required for students admitted on an equivalent qualification from a foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau school that ends at the level of Taiwan's second year of senior high school, excluding military training and PE. [1]
- Military training and PE do not count toward the 12 extra credits. [1]
- The requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 48. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- At least 16 credits each semester in years one to three and at least 9 credits each semester in year four. [1]
- If you take fewer credits, you must obtain approval from your advisor and department head; otherwise you may be dismissed. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- International students must take the full-year five-credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” (僑生國文) instead of the local students’ Chinese (A) 3 credits and Chinese (B) 2 credits. [1]
- Students who take the “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” are not required to take “Chinese (B): Chinese Writing.” [1]
- The requirement is 5 credits of Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center [1]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) for details [1]
- Visit https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [1]

- Students must complete five semesters of physical education (PE) (Freshman PE I, Freshman PE II, and three PE interest electives) [1]
- These five semesters do not count toward graduation credits [1]
- After completing the five semesters, students may take an additional 1‑credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation credits [1]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [1]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU; waived courses do not count. [1]

- At least 34 credits, of which at least 18 are doctoral-level, not counting dissertation credits. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 for more information. [1]
- The relevant regulation is National Central University Study Regulations, Article 58. [1]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester [1]
- If approved, you skip both semesters and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 for assistance [1]
- The application process is case‑by‑case for students from English‑speaking countries [1]

- Undergraduates must complete at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before receiving the degree certificate. [1]

- The website is https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [1]

- Service learning is not listed among the graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students. [1]
- The graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students are courses and credits, the degree examination, and conduct grades. [1]
- Individual departments may still set their own requirements. [1]
- National Central University Study Regulations, Article 64: Postgraduate students meeting the following requirements shall graduate immediately. [1]
